A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Gatekeeper research despite retitling and extensive reformatting. Their complete main texts, equations, figures and appendices support comparison; v1's background and experimental appendices are retained within v2's reorganized appendices.

before.justification: Section 4 and Figures 4–7 report original image-classification, language-model and vision-language experiments. Appendix B includes additional empirical analyses.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the original experiments and adds evaluated comparators. Appendix C retains the empirical confidence-separation, deferral and accuracy analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same alpha-weighted cross-entropy loss for correct predictions and uniform-target KL loss for incorrect predictions, including the token-wise extension. Max-softmax and negative-entropy routing remain unchanged; rewritten explanations do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate CIFAR-10/100, Food-101, TinyImageNet200, ARC-e/c, MMLU, GSM8K, VQAv2, AI2D, Cococap and Screen2Words. The added comparisons use retained datasets and tasks; no new domain or test scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: Figure 4 adds Narasimhan et al. (2022) across the four image-classification datasets, and Figure 6 adds Gupta et al. (2024) across the four language benchmarks. These previously cited methods become evaluated comparators, substantially extending comparison beyond untuned and prompting baselines.

E3.justification: The model pairs, alpha sweeps, metrics and training framework are retained. Section 4.2 narrows 'validation/test' to 'validation' without identifying a replacement partition; this refines documentation rather than establishing a changed split. No distinct protocol or budget revision is specified for the added comparisons.

E4.justification: The accuracy-deferral trade-off analysis in Figure 5 and the ROC, confidence-distribution, deferral-curve and fixed-deferral-ratio analyses in Figures 9–12 are retained. No new ablation, robustness test or case study is added.

E5.justification: Both versions report performance estimates and curves without experimental repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added comparator results do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figures 4 and 6 add substantial comparative results for Narasimhan et al. and Gupta et al., showing stronger deferral alternatives than the original untuned baselines while retaining lower-alpha Gatekeeper's deferral advantage. The existing Gatekeeper and prompting results, VLM results and appendix curves remain unchanged; this is expanded comparative evidence, not improved same-method performance.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 softens the error-nesting premise: v1 states that mistakes made by the large model are also made by the small model, whereas v2 says they are 'likely' shared. Equations 1–12 and the ideal-deferral derivation, moved from Appendix A.2 to B.3, remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction drops the explicit CIFAR-100 improvement factor and replaces separate 7×/10× ARC-e/c factors with an 'up to 10×' headline. This narrows the quantitative summary; the central claims about an architecture-agnostic confidence-tuning loss and improved cascade deferral remain intact.

C2.justification: Section 5 replaces the limited-baseline-comparison limitation with a substantive warning that exact-token penalties can suppress semantically valid alternatives. New Appendix A discusses unequal service from deferral thresholds and fallible fallback models. Section 4.1 also adds an interpretation concerning competing methods' architectural complexity.

D1.justification: V2 specifies validation evaluation more narrowly but abbreviates training documentation, omitting v1's explicit instruction-tuned starting checkpoints and standard perplexity-minimization statement. The CNN listing, prompting instructions and factuality-scoring recipe remain unchanged in Appendix C. Implementation recipes for the added comparators are not supplied.

R1.justification: New Appendix B.1 substantially expands coverage of LLM routing, cascade learning, confidence calibration and confidence verbalization, adding works such as Ding, Shnitzer, Nie, Geng, Azaria, Lin, Liu and Mahaut. Several introductory references are removed, while the central positioning relative to outlier exposure and static data partitioning is retained.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper GATEKEEPER and extensively rewrites and compresses the introduction, related work, method explanation and experimental narrative. It also reorganizes the appendices around new broader-impact and related-work sections. These are substantial language and structural revisions beyond the scientific additions.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a different document template and broadly revises figure presentation: Figure 3 becomes horizontal and recolored, Figures 4 and 6 gain comparator bars and large-model accuracy references, and Figure 7 is compressed with revised axes. Figure 3's caption incorrectly retains the previous color descriptions.

improvement.justification: The evaluated cascade baselines in Figures 4 and 6 partially address v1's acknowledged comparison weakness. Expanded research context, tighter exposition and the semantic-token limitation also improve the paper. These gains are tempered by sparse implementation information for the new comparators, some lost training detail and Figure 3's new caption-color mismatch, yielding a limited net improvement.
